## About 816800.xyz

> Source: https://816800.xyz/about/

Last updated: September 19, 2026
816800.xyz is a **pure front-end, ad-free** minimal tech toolkit. We gather the scattered small tools developers use daily into one unified, restrained, high-quality dark interface — "open, use, done."
### Why we exist
When debugging streams, parsing JSON or compressing images, developers often jump between sites full of popups and tracking scripts. We believe a tool should be like a Swiss Army knife — sharp, reliable, unobtrusive. This site runs no auto-ads and injects no tracking pixels; every core feature runs locally in your browser.
### How our tools are built
Every tool here follows the same three rules, which explain most of our design decisions:
- **No build step, no framework.** Hand-written HTML, one hand-tuned CSS file and vanilla JavaScript. There is no bundler to break and no large runtime to download before the tool becomes usable.
- **Vendor libraries are served locally.** `hls.js`, `dash.js` and `Plyr` live in `/assets/vendor/` on our own domain, so no third-party CDN can inject code into your session or log your address.
- **Computation happens on your device.** Text conversion, word counting, font mapping and stream decoding all run inside the browser tab. Your input is never uploaded anywhere to be processed.
### Tech stack
- **Static hosting**: Cloudflare Pages global CDN — zero server cost, high concurrency, and naturally resistant to defacement.
- **Front-end**: pure static HTML5 + a hand-crafted dark-theme CSS, zero redundant bundling, Core Web Vitals by default.
- **Player core**: hls.js decodes M3U8/HLS, dash.js decodes MPD/DASH, and Plyr provides a flat playback UI.
### What "privacy-first" actually means here
Lots of sites claim it, so here is the concrete version — what this site does, and what it never does:
| What happens | What never happens |
| --- | --- |
| Recent stream URLs and tool preferences are kept in your browser's localStorage, on your device only. | We run no user accounts, and there is nothing to sign up for. |
| The M3U8 player and text tools process what you paste locally, inside the tab. | Your URLs, text or files are not uploaded to, or stored on, our servers. |
| We measure aggregate page views with Google Analytics 4 to see which tools are worth improving. | We do not sell, rent or trade personal data, and we run no cross-site advertising trackers. |
How data is handled on 816800.xyz ``[](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/)
You can wipe everything the site has saved by clearing site data in your browser. The full legal version lives in our [privacy policy](https://816800.xyz/privacy/).
### Who these tools are for
- **Streaming engineers and QA testers** who need to confirm that an HLS or DASH manifest actually plays before shipping it.
- **Developers** who want to confirm a manifest or a stream URL without standing up a player, installing ffmpeg or writing a test page.
- **Site owners and CDN operators** checking whether a stream's `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers actually allow browser playback.
- **Anyone on a locked-down machine** where installing software is not an option — a browser is all you need.
### How we decide what to build next
A tool only gets added if it passes three tests: it solves a recurring problem we have personally hit, it can run entirely client-side, and it is meaningfully better than the ten results already ranking on page one. That last test is why the site grows slowly — roughly one new tool every one to two months rather than a batch of thin clones.
### Tool roadmap
We follow a "framework first, features unlocked in batches" strategy. The [M3U8 / HLS online player](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/) is already live; a new tool from the placeholder cards (e.g. local WebP compression, JSON conversion, QR generation) unlocks every 1–2 months to keep the site fresh.
### Frequently asked questions
#### Is everything really free?
Yes. Every tool is free, with no usage cap, no watermark and no account. We keep the whole toolkit open instead of putting features behind a login.
#### Do I need to install anything?
No. If your browser can load this page, it can run every tool on it. An up-to-date Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari gives the best results, especially for HLS and DASH playback.
#### Can I use the output commercially?
Yes. Converted text, generated short links and counting statistics are yours to use, including in commercial work. We claim no rights over what you process.
#### Something is broken — who do I tell?
Use the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/) and include the tool name, the input you used and your browser. A concrete bug report is the fastest way to get a fix prioritised.
### Who writes this site
**Wen Lau** builds and maintains 816800.xyz — the tools, the player and the documentation. That is a pen name, chosen so there is a specific person accountable for what this site says rather than an anonymous template, while keeping my personal details off the internet.
What that name is actually responsible for:
| Area | What it means concretely |
| --- | --- |
| Streaming tools | Maintains the M3U8/HLS and MPD/DASH player, its CORS diagnostics and the test source list. Public test streams are re-checked periodically and replaced when they stop responding |
| Written documentation | Writes and revises every guide here. Wherever a guide quotes a number — latency, bitrate, response time, error codes — it came from a request run against a real endpoint, not from summarising a specification |
| Stream diagnosis | Implements the CORS probe, error mapping and test-source checks in the player so a failure is attributed to a specific cause rather than a blank screen |
| Corrections | Owns factual errors in this content. If something here is wrong, report it and the page gets fixed with an updated revision date |
Working areas beyond this site: HTTP adaptive streaming (HLS, LL-HLS, MPEG-DASH), browser media APIs including Media Source Extensions, and front-end tooling that runs without a backend. Every measurement published on 816800.xyz is dated and describes the conditions it was taken under, because a number without conditions is not evidence.
### How we test and publish
Everything here is written and checked by the one person named above, so the process is short enough to state plainly. These are the rules this site actually follows — hold us to them.
| Rule | What it means in practice |
| --- | --- |
| Measured beats cited | Any number printed here — playlist size, segment duration, time to first frame, response codes — came from a request run against a public endpoint. If a figure comes from reading a specification instead, the sentence says so explicitly. |
| Test sources get re-checked | The four public streams offered as quick-test links are probed periodically. When one stops responding, the entry is replaced or removed rather than left to fail silently in front of a visitor. |
| Every page carries a revision date | Each tool and guide shows Last updated at the top and mirrors it into structured data. A page whose content changed without its date changing is a bug. |
| No payment for placement | No tool appears in any comparison on this site because someone paid for the position. There are no affiliate slots in these lists, and there is no sponsored content. |
| No bulk generation | Guides are written one at a time against a specific question we have seen break something. Pages are not generated from keyword spreadsheets, and thin pages get rewritten rather than left in place. |
| Corrections are visible | A factual error reported through the contact page gets fixed, the revision date moves, and non-trivial corrections are noted on the changelog. Silently editing away a mistake is not how this works. |
**
Where a claim rests on somebody else's specification, we link to that source instead of paraphrasing it. The [stream tester](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/) and its guides cite [RFC 8216](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8216), [Apple's HLS documentation](https://developer.apple.com/streaming/), [MDN on CORS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS), and the [hls.js](https://github.com/video-dev/hls.js) and [dash.js](https://github.com/Dash-Industry-Forum/dash.js) source trees, because those are the documents the software itself conforms to.
### Contact us
Any suggestions or want to request priority for a tool? Reach us via the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/).

## Contact

> Source: https://816800.xyz/contact/

Last updated: September 19, 2026
We value every message
Have a tool idea, hit an error, or want to request priority for a feature? Fill in the form below and it will open in your email client to reach us (this is a pure static site, so the form never passes through a server — privacy guaranteed).
### What we can help with
- **Bug reports** — a tool returned the wrong result, froze, or failed to load a stream.
- **Stream debugging** — an M3U8 or MPD URL refuses to play and you want a second opinion on whether the manifest, the codec or CORS is at fault.
- **Feature requests** — a tool you wish existed, or an option missing from one that does.
- **Content corrections** — something in a guide is out of date, inaccurate or missing a step.
- **Link exchange and partnerships** — see the criteria on our [friends page](https://816800.xyz/links/).
### What to include so we can actually help
The single biggest cause of a slow fix is a report we cannot reproduce. Copy this checklist into your message:
1. Which tool or page, with the full URL if you have it.
1. The exact input — the stream address, the pasted text, or the file type.
1. What you expected, and what actually happened.
1. Your browser and operating system, for example "Firefox 141 on Windows 11".
1. Any error text from the page or the browser console.
For stream problems, the [M3U8 player](https://816800.xyz/m3u8-player/) prints a built-in diagnostic that separates "URL unreachable" from "blocked by CORS". Pasting that line into your message saves a full round trip.
### Response times
| Type of message | What to expect |
| --- | --- |
| Bug report that breaks a tool | Investigated within 2–3 business days |
| Feature request | Acknowledged and added to the roadmap; shipped only if it clears our three-test bar |
| Content correction | Fixed or answered within a week |
| Link exchange | Reviewed within 1–2 weeks |
| Anything commercial | Answered as time allows — we do not sell placements |
Typical reply windows — we are a small team, so treat these as targets, not guarantees
### Frequently asked questions
#### Where does my message go?
Nowhere until you send it. This is a static site with no back end, so the form only assembles a draft inside your own email client, addressed to **admin@816800.xyz**. Nothing is written to a database, and we never see your address until you choose to send.
#### Do you offer paid support or custom tools?
Not at the moment. The toolkit is free and support is best-effort. If you need contractual response times, we are the wrong contact.
#### Can you help me play a stream that isn't mine?
We can explain why a stream fails at a technical level — CORS headers, unsupported codecs, expired tokens, geo-blocking — but we will not help circumvent access controls or DRM on content you do not own.
#### Do you accept guest posts or paid links?
No. Every guide on this site is written by us and we do not sell links. Genuine link swaps with sites we actually use are welcome; details are on the [friends page](https://816800.xyz/links/).

## Friends & Links

> Source: https://816800.xyz/links/

Recommended
Last updated: September 19, 2026
Sites and partners we trust and recommend. We link to each other to grow together.
HandyTools handytools.eu.cc Free browser-based tools that run fully on your device — private by design, no signup, no tracking. MetaAI metaai.indevs.in A directory of 788+ AI tools across 35 categories — image, writing, coding, video, audio and chatbots, with bilingual guides.
### How we choose the sites listed here
A link from us is a recommendation, so the bar is higher than "you linked to us first". Every site above was checked against the same four questions:
- **Does it actually work?** We open it and use the main feature. Broken flows, dead links or a wall of popups disqualify a site immediately.
- **Is it useful to the same reader?** Our audience is developers, streaming engineers and technical writers. A well-made tool or a genuine directory fits; unrelated content does not.
- **Does it respect the visitor?** No forced signup just to try the feature, no aggressive ad layouts, and ideally work that stays on the device.
- **Is it maintained?** Something touched in the last few months, not a project abandoned years ago.
### Want to be added?
Send the site URL and one line on what it does via the [contact page](https://816800.xyz/contact/). We review requests within one to two weeks and reply either way — a silent no is not how we work.
We do not require a reciprocal link and we do not accept payment for placement. If your site is a good fit we will list it whether or not you link back; if it isn't, no amount of link swapping changes that.
### Frequently asked questions
#### Do I have to link back to 816800.xyz?
No. A reciprocal link is welcome but never a condition. We would rather list a genuinely useful site than trade favours.
#### My site is listed but has changed since then.
Tell us and we will update or remove the entry. Listings are reviewed periodically, but we would rather hear it from you first.
#### Do you list competitors?
Yes, if they are good. A reader who needs a working tool matters more to us than defending a keyword.
#### Why are there only two sites here?
Because we would rather have two links we stand behind than twenty that pad the page. The list grows when we find something worth recommending, not on a schedule.
Want to swap links? [Get in touch](https://816800.xyz/contact/).
